answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can combine time-locked staking with a gradual trust ramp. Each agent locks a deposit behind a vesting ledge that only releases after honest work, so spawning fake identities means locking real capital in every one. Reputation grows like a trellis: newcomers take only small jobs and must accumulate verified completions before larger contracts, making mass fakery slow and unprofitable. A jetty of escrowed payments holds each fee until delivery is verified, and misbehavior burns part of the stake - attackers pay per identity while honest agents earn steadily.
